reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space (with its induced norm), let f:E→ℝ, let X,Y:ℝ→E, and let α,T∈ℝ. Suppose α≥0 and T≥0, f is Fréchet differentiable at every point of E, and f is globally α-strongly convex in the convention f((1−λ)x+λy)≤(1−λ)f(x)+λf(y)−(α/2)λ(1−λ)‖y−x‖² for all x,y∈E and λ∈[0,1]. Suppose X and Y are continuous on [0,T] in the relative topology. For every t∈[0,T), suppose their right derivatives exist, using the domain [t,∞), and satisfy X′₊(t)=−∇f(X(t)) and Y′₊(t)=−∇f(Y(t)), where ∇f is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative. Then for every t∈[0,T], ‖Y(t)−X(t)‖≤exp(−αt)‖Y(0)−X(0)‖. Both the initial and final endpoints are included in the conclusion. No derivative condition at T is assumed; if T=0 the derivative assumptions are empty. No finite-dimensionality, continuity of the derivative, Lipschitz gradient, minimizer, or global existence assertion is imposed.
objects: E, f, X, Y, α, T; gradient determined by the real inner product
domains: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space; f:E→ℝ; X,Y:ℝ→E; α,T∈[0,∞)
quantifiers: Universal over E, its indicated structures, f, X, Y, α,T, subject to the hypotheses; derivative hypotheses for every t∈[0,T); conclusion for every t∈[0,T].
assumptions: Global Fréchet differentiability and global α-strong convexity of f; relative continuity of both trajectories on [0,T]; right gradient-flow derivatives at all times in [0,T).
scopes: Spatial assumptions hold on all E. Derivative assumptions use right half-lines [t,∞) at t<T. Trajectory continuity and conclusion include t=T. Values of trajectories outside [0,T] are otherwise unrestricted.
constant_dependencies: Exponential rate is the supplied nonnegative strong-convexity parameter α; multiplicative constant is exactly the initial separation, with no additional constants.
